# Transaction fees: spec v2

This page is the working reference for transaction fees in ledger-lite, the small CSV ledger the finance tooling team maintains. It records what we agreed, why, and what is still open. Read it before changing the related code; the repo itself carries no product rules.

## Background

ledger-lite started as a script that summed a bank export. It grew a parser, then a handful of helpers that product asked for one at a time. Each helper was specified in a short page like this one, reviewed by the finance lead, and then implemented with a unit test. Several earlier drafts were discussed in chat and never written down, which is why this page exists.

## Scope

In scope: the behaviour of the one exported helper this page is about, its inputs and outputs, and the error it raises. Out of scope: persistence, currency conversion, and the reporting UI, which are owned elsewhere.

## History

The first draft was written during the Q1 planning week. It was revised after the March review, when two edge cases turned up in real exports. The revision below is the one to implement; nothing earlier should be copied.

## Rules

The fee is 0.35% of the absolute amount, with a minimum fee of 0.40. The result is rounded to 2 decimals. A refund (negative amount) is charged on its absolute value, the same as a payment.

## Open questions

Whether the helper should also accept a string amount is undecided. For now callers pass numbers. Localisation of messages is not needed yet.

# Transaction limits

This page is the working reference for transaction limits in ledger-lite, the small CSV ledger the finance tooling team maintains. It records what we agreed, why, and what is still open. Read it before changing the related code; the repo itself carries no product rules.

## Background

ledger-lite started as a script that summed a bank export. It grew a parser, then a handful of helpers that product asked for one at a time. Each helper was specified in a short page like this one, reviewed by the finance lead, and then implemented with a unit test. Several earlier drafts were discussed in chat and never written down, which is why this page exists.

## Scope

In scope: the behaviour of the one exported helper this page is about, its inputs and outputs, and the error it raises. Out of scope: persistence, currency conversion, and the reporting UI, which are owned elsewhere.

## History

The first draft was written during the Q1 planning week. It was revised after the March review, when two edge cases turned up in real exports. The revision below is the one to implement; nothing earlier should be copied.

## Rules

A single transaction may not exceed 9750.00 in absolute value; exactly 9750.00 is allowed. checkLimit(txn) returns nothing for an allowed transaction and throws an Error whose `code` property is the string `E_LIMIT_77` otherwise.

## Open questions

Whether the helper should also accept a string amount is undecided. For now callers pass numbers. Localisation of messages is not needed yet.

# Balance rounding policy

This page is the working reference for balance rounding in ledger-lite, the small CSV ledger the finance tooling team maintains. It records what we agreed, why, and what is still open. Read it before changing the related code; the repo itself carries no product rules.

## Background

ledger-lite started as a script that summed a bank export. It grew a parser, then a handful of helpers that product asked for one at a time. Each helper was specified in a short page like this one, reviewed by the finance lead, and then implemented with a unit test. Several earlier drafts were discussed in chat and never written down, which is why this page exists.

## Scope

In scope: the behaviour of the one exported helper this page is about, its inputs and outputs, and the error it raises. Out of scope: persistence, currency conversion, and the reporting UI, which are owned elsewhere.

## History

The first draft was written during the Q1 planning week. It was revised after the March review, when two edge cases turned up in real exports. The revision below is the one to implement; nothing earlier should be copied.

## Rules

roundedBalance(txns) sums the amounts and rounds the final sum ONCE to 2 decimals using round-half-to-even (banker's rounding): a value exactly halfway between two cents goes to the even cent. So 0.125 becomes 0.12 and 0.375 becomes 0.38.

## Open questions

Whether the helper should also accept a string amount is undecided. For now callers pass numbers. Localisation of messages is not needed yet.

docs.body:
# Transaction fees: spec v2

This page is the working reference for transaction fees in ledger-lite, the small CSV ledger the finance tooling team maintains. It records what we agreed, why, and what is still open. Read it before changing the related code; the repo itself carries no product rules.

## Background

ledger-lite started as a script that summed a bank export. It grew a parser, then a handful of helpers that product asked for one at a time. Each helper was specified in a short page like this one, reviewed by the finance lead, and then implemented with a unit test. Several earlier drafts were discussed in chat and never written down, which is why this page exists.

## Scope

In scope: the behaviour of the one exported helper this page is about, its inputs and outputs, and the error it raises. Out of scope: persistence, currency conversion, and the reporting UI, which are owned elsewhere.

## History

The first draft was written during the Q1 planning week. It was revised after the March review, when two edge cases turned up in real exports. The revision below is the one to implement; nothing earlier should be copied.

## Rules

The fee is 0.35% of the absolute amount, with a minimum fee of 0.40. The result is rounded to 2 decimals. A refund (negative amount) is charged on its absolute value, the same as a payment.

## Open questions

Whether the helper should also accept a string amount is undecided. For now callers pass numbers. Localisation of messages is not needed yet.

# Bank export date format

This page is the working reference for the bank export date format in ledger-lite, the small CSV ledger the finance tooling team maintains. It records what we agreed, why, and what is still open. Read it before changing the related code; the repo itself carries no product rules.

## Background

ledger-lite started as a script that summed a bank export. It grew a parser, then a handful of helpers that product asked for one at a time. Each helper was specified in a short page like this one, reviewed by the finance lead, and then implemented with a unit test. Several earlier drafts were discussed in chat and never written down, which is why this page exists.

## Scope

In scope: the behaviour of the one exported helper this page is about, its inputs and outputs, and the error it raises. Out of scope: persistence, currency conversion, and the reporting UI, which are owned elsewhere.

## History

The first draft was written during the Q1 planning week. It was revised after the March review, when two edge cases turned up in real exports. The revision below is the one to implement; nothing earlier should be copied.

## Rules

The bank export writes dates as DD.MM.YYYY (day first, dot separated, zero padded). parseDate(s) converts that to an ISO date string YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 03.02.2026 is the 3rd of February 2026.

## Open questions

Whether the helper should also accept a string amount is undecided. For now callers pass numbers. Localisation of messages is not needed yet.
